questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L01 Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Scenario: A student will speak to classmates about using a homework checklist. What is the clearest purpose? \

answer.text: A. To describe every assignment from the week

feedback.text: Incorrect. That would list information, but the scenario focuses on a checklist habit.

answer.text: B. To entertain classmates with a story about homework

feedback.text: Incorrect. Nothing in the scenario suggests the purpose is entertainment.

answer.text: C. To explain how a checklist can help classmates manage homework

feedback.text: Correct. This purpose fits the audience and explains what the speaker wants listeners to understand.

answer.text: D. To compare school rules from different classes

feedback.text: Incorrect. The task is about a homework checklist, not comparing rules.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L01 Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.L.01 Scenario: Audience: school administrators. Topic: adding a tutoring table after school. Which wording best fits the audience? \

answer.text: A. An after-school tutoring table could provide targeted academic support for students who need help before going home.

feedback.text: Correct. This is formal, specific, and appropriate for administrators.

answer.text: B. We really need this because students are stressed.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is understandable but too general for an administrator audience.

answer.text: C. Tutoring is a thing people probably want.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and informal, so it weakens the message.

answer.text: D. Everybody should just agree to make tutoring happen.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This sounds demanding and does not show audience awareness.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L01 Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.R.10 Scenario: Topic: reading before bed. Which sentence is a clear perspective statement? \

answer.text: A. Reading before bed is the topic of my presentation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This only names the topic and does not state a perspective.

answer.text: B. Many books can be read at night.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a general detail, not a guiding perspective.

answer.text: C. Some people read and some people do not.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a vague observation and does not guide a presentation.

answer.text: D. Reading before bed can help students create a calmer routine before sleep.

feedback.text: Correct. This sentence gives a clear point of view about the topic.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.V.01 U06 L01 Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.01 Scenario: A student is speaking to teachers about student study routines. Which phrase uses academic vocabulary best? \

answer.text: A. Getting stuff done faster

feedback.text: Incorrect. The phrase is informal and too vague for a prepared presentation.

answer.text: B. Developing effective study routines

feedback.text: Correct. This phrase uses clear academic vocabulary appropriate for a teacher audience.

answer.text: C. Doing school things better

feedback.text: Incorrect. This wording is general and does not communicate a precise idea.

answer.text: D. Figuring out all the homework stuff

feedback.text: Incorrect. This phrase is informal and unclear.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L01 Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Scenario: A speaker says, "My topic is lunch." What is missing? \

answer.text: A. A shorter topic

feedback.text: Incorrect. The problem is not that the topic is too long; it is too unfocused.

answer.text: B. A list of all audience members

feedback.text: Incorrect. Knowing the audience helps, but the immediate problem is lack of purpose and perspective.

answer.text: C. A clear purpose and perspective

feedback.text: Correct. The sentence names a topic but does not explain what the speaker will do or what point the speaker will make.

answer.text: D. A direct quote from a source

feedback.text: Incorrect. Evidence may come later, but the topic first needs a clear direction.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L01 Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.L.01 Scenario: A student will speak to younger students about staying organized. Which audience detail is most useful for planning? \

answer.text: A. The room has a projector.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The room may affect delivery, but it does not describe the listeners' needs.

answer.text: B. The listeners are new to managing several class assignments.

feedback.text: Correct. This detail helps the speaker choose examples and language that fit the audience.

answer.text: C. The presentation happens on Tuesday.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The date is not as useful as knowing the audience's experience.

answer.text: D. The speaker owns a planner.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is about the speaker, not the audience.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L01 Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.R.10 Scenario: Purpose: persuade classmates to try a school club. Which opening best matches the purpose? \

answer.text: A. There are school clubs at many schools.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too general and does not persuade classmates to try one.

answer.text: B. My presentation includes three slides.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This describes the presentation format, not the persuasive purpose.

answer.text: C. Clubs are listed on the school website.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This detail may be useful later, but it does not state a persuasive point.

answer.text: D. Joining one school club can help you meet people and feel more connected at school.

feedback.text: Correct. This opening gives a persuasive perspective that fits classmates.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.L.01 U06 L01 Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.01 Scenario: A speaker's note says, "Students needs clear routines when they starts high school." Which revision is correct for standard English? \

answer.text: A. Students need clear routines when they start high school.

feedback.text: Correct. Both verbs agree with their subjects, making the statement clear.

answer.text: B. Students needs clear routines when they start high school.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The verb "needs" still does not agree with the plural subject "Students."

answer.text: C. Student need clear routines when they starts high school.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This version creates number and agreement problems.

answer.text: D. Students needing clear routines when starting high school.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a fragment and does not make a complete statement.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L01 Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Scenario: A student is presenting to parents about digital calendars. Which perspective is most audience-aware? \

answer.text: A. Digital calendars are better than paper all the time.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too absolute and does not focus on the parent audience.

answer.text: B. Some students have phones and some do not.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a detail but not a focused perspective for parents.

answer.text: C. Calendars have boxes for dates.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too obvious and does not explain why the audience should care.

answer.text: D. Digital calendars can help families support students by making due dates visible at home.

feedback.text: Correct. This perspective connects the topic to a parent audience.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L01 Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.L.01 Scenario: A speaker wants to inform classmates about the steps for joining a club. Which purpose statement is strongest? \

answer.text: A. I will tell some things about clubs.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and does not identify the specific information listeners need.

answer.text: B. Clubs are fun after school.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is more of an opinion than a clear informational purpose.

answer.text: C. I will explain the steps classmates can follow to join a school club.

feedback.text: Correct. This purpose is specific, audience-aware, and informational.

answer.text: D. Students sometimes join clubs.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a statement of fact, not a strong purpose.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L01 Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.R.10 Scenario: Topic: school announcements. Audience: new students. Which perspective is clearest? \

answer.text: A. School announcements happen every day.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a detail, not a perspective.

answer.text: B. Listening to school announcements can help new students learn important routines and opportunities.

feedback.text: Correct. This gives a clear point of view that fits the audience.

answer.text: C. New students are at school.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain the topic or the speaker's point.

answer.text: D. I will talk about announcements.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This names the topic but does not state a perspective.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.R.10 U06 L01 Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.01 Text: "Students who explain ideas in their own words often notice what they understand and where they need more review." Which paraphrase is best for a speaker? \

answer.text: A. Restating ideas helps students check their understanding and find gaps.

feedback.text: Correct. This keeps the meaning while using new wording.

answer.text: B. Students explain ideas and notice all things.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and loses important meaning from the original text.

answer.text: C. Students should memorize every sentence exactly.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This contradicts the idea of explaining in one's own words.

answer.text: D. Review is unnecessary when students explain ideas.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This reverses the meaning because the text says explanation can show where review is needed.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L01 Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Scenario: A presentation is for classmates who already know the topic. What should the speaker do? \

answer.text: A. Repeat only basic definitions the audience already knows.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That does not respect the audience's existing knowledge.

answer.text: B. Avoid having a clear perspective.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A clear perspective is still needed, even when the audience knows the topic.

answer.text: C. Use examples and details that extend what the audience already understands.

feedback.text: Correct. Audience awareness means adjusting depth and examples for listeners.

answer.text: D. Make the presentation less organized.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Organization remains important for any audience.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L01 Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.L.01 Scenario: A speaker will recommend that students use the library database. Which audience is most specific? \

answer.text: A. People

feedback.text: Incorrect. This audience is too broad to guide language or examples.

answer.text: B. Everyone at school

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is still broad and does not show who specifically needs the message.

answer.text: C. Anyone who hears it

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not help the speaker plan an audience-aware message.

answer.text: D. Ninth-grade students beginning their first research assignment

feedback.text: Correct. This audience is specific enough to shape examples and vocabulary.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.V.01 U06 L01 Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.R.10 Scenario: A student is replacing informal wording in a presentation. Which revision is most academic? \

answer.text: A. "Useful strategy" instead of "good thing to try"

feedback.text: Correct. "Useful strategy" is precise and appropriate for academic speaking.

answer.text: B. "A bunch of stuff" instead of "several resources"

feedback.text: Incorrect. This revision moves from precise to vague language.

answer.text: C. "Kinda helps" instead of "supports"

feedback.text: Incorrect. This makes the language less academic and less precise.

answer.text: D. "Things we do" instead of "routines"

feedback.text: Incorrect. This weakens the vocabulary and makes the meaning less clear.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L01 Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.01 Scenario: Which plan best shows purpose, audience, and perspective? \

answer.text: A. Topic: attendance. I will talk for one minute.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This includes topic and time but no audience or perspective.

answer.text: B. I will explain to classmates how organized notes can make studying easier.

feedback.text: Correct. This includes purpose, audience, and perspective.

answer.text: C. Topic: note-taking. People should listen.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too vague and does not clearly identify the audience or perspective.

answer.text: D. My slides will have blue titles and pictures.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This focuses on visuals, not the communication plan.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L01 Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Scenario: A speaker is addressing community volunteers. Which tone is most appropriate? \

answer.text: A. Sarcastic and careless

feedback.text: Incorrect. This tone would weaken trust and distract from the message.

answer.text: B. Confusing and rushed

feedback.text: Incorrect. A rushed tone makes it harder for listeners to follow.

answer.text: C. Respectful and clear

feedback.text: Correct. Community volunteers need a tone that is polite, understandable, and prepared.

answer.text: D. Overly casual and vague

feedback.text: Incorrect. Casual language may not fit a community audience or a formal task.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L01 Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.L.01 Scenario: A student says, "Everyone knows this already." What planning problem does this show? \

answer.text: A. The speaker has chosen too many sources.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The issue is not source quantity; it is audience assumptions.

answer.text: B. The speaker has used too much standard English.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Standard English is not the problem.

answer.text: C. The speaker has written a clear perspective.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The statement does not show a clear perspective.

answer.text: D. The speaker is assuming audience knowledge without checking it.

feedback.text: Correct. Speakers should consider what listeners know and need.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L01 Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.R.10 Scenario: Topic: healthy snacks. Audience: students before practice. Which perspective fits best? \

answer.text: A. Snacks are food people eat.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too obvious and does not provide a useful perspective.

answer.text: B. There are many snacks in the world.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is broad and not audience-aware.

answer.text: C. Choosing a simple snack before practice can help students stay focused and energized.

feedback.text: Correct. This perspective fits the student-athlete audience and gives a clear point.

answer.text: D. Practice happens after school.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a detail, not a focused perspective.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.L.01 U06 L01 Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.01 Scenario: Which sentence is best for a prepared oral presentation? \

answer.text: A. Our routines helps us because they keeps us focused.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The verbs do not agree with the plural subjects.

answer.text: B. Routines, they help focus because focus is helped.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This sentence is awkward and unclear.

answer.text: C. Routines helping students focus during the week.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a fragment, not a complete sentence.

answer.text: D. Consistent routines help students stay focused during the week.

feedback.text: Correct. This sentence uses standard English and communicates clearly.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L01 Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Scenario: A speaker is presenting to classmates about peer tutoring. Which purpose is strongest? \

answer.text: A. To explain how peer tutoring can help students review difficult concepts

feedback.text: Correct. This purpose is specific and fits an oral presentation to classmates.

answer.text: B. To say peer tutoring exists

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too limited and does not explain what listeners should understand.

answer.text: C. To read every tutoring schedule aloud

feedback.text: Incorrect. That would overload listeners with details instead of giving a focused purpose.

answer.text: D. To avoid giving a clear opinion

feedback.text: Incorrect. A presentation needs a clear perspective or purpose.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L01 Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.L.01 Scenario: Which sentence best shows audience awareness for new ninth-grade students? \

answer.text: A. Students of all ages have always had school responsibilities.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is broad and less useful for new ninth-grade students.

answer.text: B. When you have several classes for the first time, a weekly checklist can help you track what each teacher expects.

feedback.text: Correct. This sentence connects directly to the audience's likely experience.

answer.text: C. I personally like checklists better than everything else.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This focuses on the speaker rather than the audience.

answer.text: D. Organization is a word with many meanings.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not address the audience's needs.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L01 Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.R.10 Scenario: A student writes, "My purpose is to inform, my audience is classmates, and my perspective is that study groups can make review less stressful." What is the best evaluation? \

answer.text: A. The plan is missing an audience.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The audience is clearly identified as classmates.

answer.text: B. The plan includes purpose, audience, and perspective.

feedback.text: Correct. All three planning parts are present and connected.

answer.text: C. The plan has only a topic and no perspective.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The sentence includes a clear perspective about study groups.

answer.text: D. The plan should remove the purpose.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The purpose is needed to guide the presentation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L01 Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.01 Scenario: Which presentation topic has been turned into the strongest perspective? \

answer.text: A. Eating school breakfast can help students begin the day prepared to learn.

feedback.text: Correct. This is a clear perspective that can guide the presentation.

answer.text: B. Topic: school breakfast.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is only a topic and does not state a point of view.

answer.text: C. School breakfast happens before classes.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a detail, not a perspective.

answer.text: D. I will talk about school breakfast.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This names the task but does not provide a focused point.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L01 Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Scenario: A student has a clear perspective but no audience. What should the student do next? \

answer.text: A. Remove the perspective from the plan.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The perspective is useful and should remain.

answer.text: B. Add unrelated facts to make the speech longer.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Length does not fix missing audience awareness.

answer.text: C. Choose visual colors before planning the message.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Design choices should not replace audience planning.

answer.text: D. Identify the listeners so the examples and tone can fit them.

feedback.text: Correct. Audience shapes language, examples, and tone in oral communication.
